source_evidence: Investing is when you put your money into assets such as stocks or bonds, often held in a brokerage or advisory account, with the expectation of making a return over time.
answer: Investing means putting money into assets—such as stocks or bonds—with the expectation of earning a return over time. A return may come from an asset increasing in value or from interest or dividend payments. Unlike a savings account used for short-term goals or emergencies, investments can fluctuate in value, and all investments involve some risk. Investing therefore offers the possibility of growth, but does not guarantee a particular return.
